scope: Fresh-P300-session balanced PrefixRead discriminator for KMBUS_EEPROM_READ 0x43 at local 0x0001/1.
conclusions: The earlier same-session 88 -> 87 -> 88 P-N-P pattern does not reproduce when every request is placed in a fresh P300 session.
Prefixed and no-prefix requests produced exactly the same empirical distribution: 0x81 three times and 0x87 once in each group.
The local 0x0001/1 result is therefore session/time/state dependent, not demonstrated to be controlled by the six extra PrefixRead bytes.
The prior claim that PrefixRead was hardware-proven to alter local 0x43 routing is withdrawn.
The strongest current statement is that the controller accepts extra request bytes after BlockLength, while their semantics on local VDensHO1/20C2 remain unproven.
Combined with the repeated two-byte high-address responses, local 0x43 must not be treated as a literal EEPROM dump or as validated LGM27 persistent-memory access.
source_reassessment: The public InsideViessmannVitosoft parser preserves PrefixRead as XML metadata; its byte-conversion code is commented out.
The public VS2Message builder supports optional Data bytes after BlockSize, but no recovered source currently binds the ecnEventType PrefixRead field to that Data parameter.
Therefore the mapping 'PrefixRead -> trailing VS2 request Data bytes' remains a plausible inference, not a recovered Vitosoft implementation fact.
next_step: Stop further live 0x43 address expansion for now.
Recover the actual Vitosoft host binding from PrefixRead/PrefixWrite metadata into the communication request builder using the private archive/decompiled assemblies.
Resume live 0x43 testing only after the exact vendor serialization path is recovered or another independent protocol source establishes the field placement.
